newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures quietly up, forwards shine.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures quietly up, forwards shine.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures ended Friday with pared gains after a relatively quiet session which saw some light buying interest in the back months.

Traders said one major trade house was active, buying some 500 lots in July, September and November. The buying in the deferred months helped tightnen switches with May/July trading at $5. July/Sept and May/Sept structures were also active.
By the finish, May stood $8 higher at $1,663 after ranging between $1,655 and $1,670. Other positions added $5 to $12.
Volume reached an unimpressive 3,463 lots. "This must be one of the most quiet days in coffee," said one. New York arabica futures ambled higher but rangebound.

Traders said the market was trying to digest news of a hike in arabica exports. While the supply tightness might loosen up in the short-term following the move by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries, the long-term supply concerns linger.

The ACPC agreed late on Thursday to release an additional 200,000 bags of washed arabica coffee and revoke an earlier export quota of 300,000 bags for the first half of 1997 to help satisfy roaster demand.

In addition, the ACPC has asked members to submit by April 15 proposals on coffee market stabilisation plans for consideration at an ACPC council meeting in May. The current one-year export quota programme is due to run out by the end of June.
Elsewhere, the Colombian truck drivers union is due to meet on Saturday to set the date for a nationwide strike.
Looking ahead, traders said the coffee market could see a further spike on the downside with New York retracing more than London, the latter being supported by good roaster buying.
"It's still a $1,600-$1,700 market," said one trader, referring to London's May contract. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
